summary: The affine-tube construction is valid. For each supported edge, the two quarter-radius hypotheses place the common shift in (1/2)D_*, so the shifted endpoint metronoid points have the claimed affine-graph midpoint. The source-orientation argument proves halfspace domination without pooling coincident target atoms, the dominated-measure theorem gives residual rank zero and the rank-sensitive D bound, and the same support yields a realizable reservoir submatching of mass B_{w,a}/16. Adding the distinct R and D summands is legitimate. The specialization to full good-edge weights, all strict numerical estimates, the defect comparison, the application of the triangle-backed O-branch inequality, and the affine-tube covering lower bound K>=19 all follow with the stated quantifiers and constants, including zero-mass and boundary cases.
